videos.title: 1st South Pole Expedition by Indian Scientists of Indian Antarctic Program
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description: The enigma of South Pole attracted indian scientists ever since setting feet on the icy continent. To commemorate Amundsen’s historical expedition to South Pole, as also to mark thirty years of Indian presence in Antarctica, the first scientific expedition to South Pole from Indian Station `Maitri’ was launched in year 2010. With the basic purpose to establish the capability of penetrating deeper into continent for conducting meaningful science, the 8 member team covered a distance of 2300 kms in 9 days with regular halts for collecting snow and ice samples reaching South Pole on 21st November 2010.
videos.note: India's first scientific expedition to the South Pole (2010), from Maitri. Short: best for the live Ask Dhruv demo.

videos.title: The Himalayan Ice Keepers
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description:
The movie highlights the Himalayan Expedition to study the glaciers of Chandra Basin in Western Himalayas. NCPOR, Goa organizes the Himalayan expedition under the aegis of the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Government of India. Tough terrain, unpredictable weather conditions, low oxygen level, etc are some of the challenges that the team faces while undertaking the expedition to study the health of glaciers. The research areas include microbiology, biogeochemical studies, climate change, remote sensing, modeling, etc. 
Lets explore more about the NCPOR's Himalayan Expedition through the movie.
videos.note: Documentary on the Chandra basin glacier expedition.

videos.title: Arctic The Indian Connection
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description: The Arctic is warming almost twice the global average. The impact of warming on Arctic processes affects the world. Changes in Arctic sea-ice affect the Indian monsoon. Therefore, NCPOR under the aegis of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India executes the Indian Arctic Expedition wherein scientists/ researchers from different R&D institutions and universities participate to understand the impact of climate change on the Arctic and its teleconnection with a tropical country like India. The Indian research base 'Himadri' in Svalbard, Arctic facilitates the expedition members to undertake research in the Arctic.
videos.note: Documentary: why the Arctic matters to India (sea ice and the monsoon).

videos.title: Into the Southern Ocean
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description:
The movie highlights the Scientific Expedition to the Indian Ocean Sector of the Southern Ocean.  
NCPOR, Goa under the aegis of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India organizes the expedition to understand the effect of climate change in the Indian Sector of Southern Ocean, the least studied sector of the Southern Ocean. 
The movie shows how the scientists/ researchers undertake their experiments/ studies inspite of the challenges posed during the expedition to one of the coldest and roughest oceans of the world.
videos.note: Documentary on the Southern Ocean expedition. An earlier 37-min upload exists (JJozS7XatQ8); use this one.

videos.title: MADICE Indo Norwegian Initiative
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description:
Mass Balance, dynamics, and climate of the central Dronning Maud Land coast, East Antarctica (MADICE) – an Indo-Norwegian research project co-funded by Research Council of Norway and Ministry of Earth Sciences, India. This project is investigating the mass balance, dynamics, and climate of the central Dronning Maud Land coast, East Antarctica. Leading institutions in respective countries are the Norwegian Polar Institute (NPI) and National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research in India (NCPOR, erstwhile NCAOR).
The objective of the project is to investigate the intricate relationship between floating ice shelves and grounded ice (known as ice rises) in central DML, East Antarctica
videos.note: MADICE: Indo-Norwegian project on the Dronning Maud Land coast (NCPOR and Norwegian Polar Institute).

videos.title: HIMANSH- NCPOR's High Altitude research station in Himalayas
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description:
HIMANSH is a dedicated Research Station established at Sutri Dhaka, Chandra Basin, Lahaul-Spiti valley of Himachal Pradesh which has an altitude of 4080m amsl. The station was unveiled on Sunday 9th October 2016.
Himansh facilitates Himalayan Cryosphere Studies in Chandra basin to study the dynamics and the rate of change of Himalayan glaciers to understand its impact on hydrology and climate.
videos.note: 50-second station introduction: use on the Himansh station page.

videos.title: National Centre for POlar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)- 2019
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description:
NCPOR, erstwhile NCAOR, is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India. Scientists from NCPOR addresses global and regional environmental issues under the umbrella of climate change by understanding the responses of processes to climate change in Antarctica, Arctic, Southern Ocean, and Himalayas-the third Pole. 
To facilitate the research in Polar regions, NCPOR established research bases in Antarctica (Maitri and Bharati), Arctic (Himadari) and Himalayas (Himansh).
videos.note: Institute overview (2019). Covers all regions; region set to antarctic like the annual reports.

videos.title: NCPOR | Celebrating 25 years of Excellence
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description:
Over the past 25 years, the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, has led pioneering research that has advanced global understanding of climate change, ocean dynamics, and geosciences. From the Icy expanses of Antarctica and the Arctic to the rugged high-altitude terrains of the Himalaya and the depths of the oceans, NCPOR has boldly explored Earth’s most extreme frontiers, strengthening India’s leadership in polar and ocean research. Today, NCPOR has reinforced its role in global climate science, unlocking the mysteries of Earth’s most extreme frontiers.

Join us on a visual journey through NCPOR’s transformative path, from its inception in 1998 and formal dedication to the nation on April 5, 2000, to 25 years of cutting-edge research spanning Antarctica, the Arctic, the Southern Ocean, the Indian Ocean, and the Himalayas

Visit us at : www.ncpor.res.in

videos.title: Chronicles of Year 2023 : A Retrospective Journey at NCPOR
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description:
Join us in a captivating journey as we look back on the incredible year that was 2023 at NCPOR (National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India. 
From groundbreaking research to adventurous expeditions, our NCPOR 2023 highlight video encapsulates the essence of our commitment to understanding and preserving the polar and oceanic environments.
This video is a glimpse of the vast landscapes and scientific activities that unfolded as we continued our mission to unravel the mysteries of the Polar Regions. Witness the tireless efforts of our dedicated team, pushing boundaries and making strides in polar and ocean realms. 
 
#NCPOR2023Highlights includes glimpse of 
a. Polar Expeditions by embarking on thrilling expeditions to the Arctic, Antarctic and Himalayas, witnessing the resilience of our researchers in extreme conditions. 

b. Collaborative Research: Celebrate the power of collaboration as NCPOR engages with international partners to foster knowledge exchange and mutual understanding. Various delegation visits, participation in national & international meetings; MoUs at national level  showcase the institute's interest in expanding their research areas/ expertise through collaborations. 

c. Educational and Outreach: Witness the impact of our outreach activities, inspiring the next generation of scientists and environmental stewards. 

As we bid farewell to 2023, we express gratitude to our team, collaborators, and supporters who have been an integral part of our journey. 

Join us in reliving the unforgettable memories of NCPOR's 2023!

videos.title: AntarcticaDay2021 AKAM
videos.credit: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, official YouTube channel
videos.license: Embedded with the YouTube player from the official NCPOR channel. Not downloaded or re-hosted.
videos.description:
National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa has organized a Painting and Short Comic Story Writing Competition to celebrate Antarctica Day 2021 and the 75 years of India's Independence (Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav). The Painting Competition was organized for the school students under the themes: 1.  Climate change in Polar Regions; 2. Pollution in Oceans; 3. Antarctica as you imagine.

We have received beautiful artwork from the school students across India. 
Through this video, we would like to showcase the creativity of the school students through their paintings. A big thanks to the jury members (Dr. Sushant Naik, Ms. Reshma Maharana, and Mr. Narayan Shridhar Pendse) for sparing their precious time in evaluating the paintings.
videos.note: School students' paintings from NCPOR's Antarctica Day 2021 competition.
